summary: Turns the search page into a client component that reads q from the URL, fetches matching products on render, and lists them.

findings.title: Hooks called after an early return
findings.description: The component returns before useState and useEffect when q is missing. React requires the same hook order on every render. When a user clears or adds q, React throws a hook-order error and the page crashes. Move the early return below the useState and useEffect calls.

findings.consequence: When a user clears or adds q, React throws a hook-order error and the page crashes.
findings.fix: Move the early return below the useState and useEffect calls.

findings.title: Effect without dependency array refetches every render
findings.description: The effect has no dependency array, so it runs after every render. Each run calls searchProducts and setResults, which triggers another render. The page sends a request to the catalog API after every render and loops as long as responses differ. Pass [query] as the dependency array so the effect runs only when q changes.

findings.title: URL query rendered as raw HTML
findings.description: The heading injects q from the URL into dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitizing it. An attacker can craft a search link that runs script in the browser of anyone who opens it. Render the query as text content instead of raw HTML.

findings.consequence: An attacker can craft a search link that runs script in the browser of anyone who opens it.
findings.fix: Render the query as text content instead of raw HTML.

findings.title: Search failure is never handled
findings.description: searchProducts throws when the API returns a non-OK status. The promise has no catch, so the rejection goes unhandled. A failed search leaves stale or empty results with no message, and the browser logs an unhandled rejection. Add a catch that records the error in state and shows it to the user.

findings.title: List items rendered without a key
findings.description: The map over results returns li elements with no key prop. Product has a stable id field that is not used. React warns on every render and may reuse the wrong DOM nodes when results change between searches. Use product.id as the key.

findings.consequence: React warns on every render and may reuse the wrong DOM nodes when results change between searches.

findings.title: Late response can overwrite newer results
findings.description: The effect does not cancel or ignore the previous request when q changes. A slow older response can resolve after a newer one. A user who types two searches quickly can see results for the earlier term under the later heading. Track a cancelled flag in the effect cleanup and skip setResults when it is set.
